trace.title: Measured resources
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Startup, readiness, and liveness ask different questions. Startup protects a slow initialization phase.

Readiness controls traffic eligibility. Liveness can trigger a restart when the process is stuck under the chosen health contract.

Do not make liveness depend on every remote service; an outage can cause a restart storm. A worker also needs a progress/processing health model, not necessarily the web app’s HTTP probe.

Resource requests affect scheduling; limits affect runtime behavior under the selected resource type. CPU throttling and memory termination can look like app bugs.

A rollout needs compatible schema, ready new pods, graceful old-pod shutdown, and an explicit rollback/data plan.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
New specification → new pods start → startup check → readiness allows traffic → old pods drain → process receives termination signal → unfinished work completes or becomes safely retryable.

Observe rollout and user-level error/latency.

If a worker is terminated after DB commit but before offset/queue acknowledgement, its replacement may repeat the item. Infrastructure shutdown and business idempotence must cooperate.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail:
A probe that requires login can fail every pod. Tight memory limits can cause repeated OOM termination.

A code rollback does not reverse a destructive migration.
